subject: Scan-ops closure log and exception lane for SOC2 / SIG review
messages:
From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@fintrust.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, security@fintrust.com
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: consolidated closure log + exceptions for SOC2 SIG questionnaire item 4.3

Kimberly / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the SIG. The FinTrust audit team needs a consolidated closure log that ties each CVE to: the scan that found it, the PR/issue that fixes it, deploy timestamp to prod, and any approved exceptions (with approver and expiry). Specifically:
- Item 4.3 in the SIG: "vulnerability management evidence"
- We need both the last 90-day cadence artifacts and a snapshot showing current open exceptions.

Please send a CSV or table that maps: CVE ID, severity, first-found (scan id + date), remediation PR/ID, deploy time, mitigation type (patch / config / compensating control), and exception approval doc if applicable.

Can you include an approved exceptions PDF and a short note on your SLA timelines for critical/high CVEs? Our reviewer will want explicit SLOs to reference in the SOC2 report.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendes
Security Engineer — FinTrust
security@fintrust.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@fintrust.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated closure log + exceptions for SOC2 SIG questionnaire item 4.3

Carlos —

Attached: redwood-scan-closure-log-20261019.csv (CSV mapping as requested) and cve-exception-approvals-20261019.pdf (signed exception approvals). Also included patch-pr-links-20261019.txt with links to GitHub PRs for each remediation. Highlights below:

- Scan coverage: authenticated weekly infrastructure scans (Nessus), bi-weekly dynamic scans for public services, and continuous SCA on dependencies. The CSV includes the scan id and scan type for each finding.
- SLA commitment: Critical (CVSS >=9.0) — remediation or compensating control within 72 hours; High (7.0–8.9) — remediation within 14 days; Medium/Low — risk-based window documented in CSV. We maintain a 24/7 on-call rotation for critical remediation pushes.
- Exceptions: when an exception is approved we include approver, business justification, compensating control (if any), and expiry date. The PDF is the signed approvals registry for active exceptions.

Let me know if you prefer a redacted CSV (no internal PR content) for auditors; we can also provide a temporary viewer link to the internal PRs if the audit team needs live evidence.

Next step: confirm format and whether the auditor needs stack traces or additional deploy artifacts (deploy job id, artifact checksum).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1-415-555-0172

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@fintrust.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated closure log + exceptions for SOC2 SIG questionnaire item 4.3

Carlos / Kimberly —

Adding a few technical clarifications for the auditor that may reduce follow-ups: 

- CVE linkage: each row in the CSV has a canonical CVE ID and a link to the originating scanner artifact. We tag scanner results with a deterministic fingerprint so repeated findings get deduplicated across runs.
- Remediation evidence: for each remediation PR we include the PR number, CI run id, and the deployment job id. Deploy job id is sufficient for auditors to validate a production rollout; we can provide a signed artifact checksum on request.
- Compensating controls: when an exception is in place we include the control owner and monitoring hooks (CloudWatch alarms, WAF rule ids, or IPS signatures) and frequency of verification. Those are called out in the PDF.
- Specific request: CVE-2026-1234 appears in our CSV as CLOSED (deploy id: deploy-20261012-822, PR: #4021). The CSV row shows first-found: 2026-09-28 (scan id: nessus-20260928-07), remediation PR link in the patch-pr-links text file, and the deploy timestamp.

Operational note: we run a rolling patch window on Tuesdays/Wednesdays between 0200–0600 PT for infra critical patches to minimize customer impact; emergency CRs are handled immediately with on-call escalation.

Attached: (same 3 files) — redwood-scan-closure-log-20261019.csv, cve-exception-approvals-20261019.pdf, patch-pr-links-20261019.txt.

If the auditor wants a one-hour walkthrough I can join and walk through the CSV and PR->deploy chain.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@fintrust.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated closure log + exceptions for SOC2 SIG questionnaire item 4.3

Kimberly / Soojin —

Received — thank you for the detailed package and the direct confirmation on CVE-2026-1234. A couple quick follow-ups from the audit queue: 
1) The auditor would like a short, signed SLA statement (can be one paragraph) confirming the SLA windows you listed for Critical and High findings to include in the SOC2 artifact bundle.
2) For any active exceptions that expire beyond 30 days, the auditor wants the compensating control verification cadence (e.g., daily log review, weekly automated check) included beside the exception in the PDF. If possible, add a one-line field in the PDF for that cadence.

If you can send the SLA paragraph and updated PDF with the cadence field by EOD tomorrow we should be able to close item 4.3. Otherwise we may ask for a short walkthrough next week.

Appreciate the speed — this format is exactly what the auditor wanted.

Best,
Carlos Mendes
Security Engineer — FinTrust
